narrative:
Based on the information provided, the model predicts that you have a 31% chance of not passing your final year. Because this probability is above the school’s threshold of 10%, you are required to take additional remedial courses to support your learning and help you succeed.

The model considered many aspects of your background and habits, but three factors stood out as most influential in shaping this prediction. The strongest positive influence in your favor was that you have not failed any classes in the past, which is consistent with the average student who is not required to take remedial courses. This history of no prior failures suggests you have the ability to succeed academically.

Another factor that worked in your favor is your clear intention to pursue higher education after graduation. Like all students in your group, this ambition signals motivation and a commitment to your studies, which typically lowers the risk of failing.

However, the most significant factor pushing the prediction toward a higher risk was your reported weekly study time. You spend less than two hours per week studying, while most students who are not required to take remedial courses dedicate at least two hours or more. This limited study time is a key reason the model identified you as needing extra support.

Given these findings, the best next step is to take advantage of the remedial courses offered. Increasing your study time and engaging with the additional resources can help you strengthen your understanding and improve your chances of passing the final year.
